# Anthropic protocol fixtures

These fixtures are normalized, synthetic examples derived from Anthropic's
official Messages, streaming Messages, tool use, vision, PDF support, extended
thinking, errors, and token-counting documentation as retrieved on 2026-07-24.

Normalization replaces message IDs, model names, token counts, tool arguments,
URLs, and all human-authored content with deterministic non-sensitive values.
Expected fixtures are hand-authored from the documented wire contract and are
never generated by `AnthropicCodec`.

`count_tokens/opencodex_v2_7_35.json` is a faithful JSON transcription of the
request body in OpenCodex commit
`97e7326f89bcfbb29a2c73250cb25eb801d066b6`,
`tests/claude-messages-endpoint.test.ts`, test
`count_tokens returns a positive estimate in the exact contract shape`. Only
TypeScript object syntax was normalized to JSON; field names and values are
unchanged. It is pinned implementation-test provenance, not a claimed live
Claude Code capture.

Exact source:
https://github.com/lidge-jun/opencodex/blob/97e7326f89bcfbb29a2c73250cb25eb801d066b6/tests/claude-messages-endpoint.test.ts

Field-by-field normalization:

- `model`: copied unchanged as `mock/test-model`.
- `system`: copied unchanged as `be brief`.
- `messages[0].role` and `messages[0].content`: copied unchanged.
- `tools[0].name` and `tools[0].input_schema`: copied unchanged.
- JavaScript property syntax and trailing commas: converted to strict JSON;
  no request fields were added, removed, reordered semantically, or redacted.

The pinned test asserts that `input_tokens` is positive rather than fixing one
tokenizer-specific value. `count_tokens/response.json` therefore records the
deterministic `37` returned by this repository's injected test counter; it is
not presented as an OpenCodex or Claude Code response capture.
